video.title: Private Database, Record Zone & CKSubscription | Day 222
video.description:
Learn to explain where CloudKit keeps records and how it tells your app about changes: Private Database, Record Zone & CKSubscription, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Private Database - The CloudKit database that only the signed-in user can read, and it uses that user's iCloud storage.
Record Zone - A named group of records inside a database, which helps CloudKit track changes.
CKSubscription - A request that asks CloudKit to send a push message when matching records change.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: iOS Private Database, Record Zone & CKSubscription | Day 222
landscape.description:
Explain Private Database, Record Zone & CKSubscription in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Private Database, Record Zone, CKSubscription 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Private Database - The CloudKit database that only the signed-in user can read, and it uses that user's iCloud storage.
한국어: Private Database: 로그인한 사용자만 읽을 수 있고 그 사용자의 iCloud 저장 공간을 쓰는 CloudKit 데이터베이스

Record Zone - A named group of records inside a database, which helps CloudKit track changes.
한국어: Record Zone: CloudKit이 변경 사항을 추적하도록 도와주는 데이터베이스 안의 이름 붙은 레코드 묶음

CKSubscription - A request that asks CloudKit to send a push message when matching records change.
한국어: CKSubscription: 조건에 맞는 레코드가 바뀌면 푸시 메시지를 보내 달라고 CloudKit에 하는 요청

landscape.hook: Can you explain Private Database, Record Zone and CKSubscription in English?

dialogue.title: Who can see my notes?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, which CloudKit database should hold personal notes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The private database. Only the signed-in user can read it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, `privateCloudDatabase`. And it uses the user's own iCloud storage, not ours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is a big plus. Can I put the records directly in it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can, but a record zone is better. It groups the records and helps CloudKit track changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used the default zone before, and changes were hard to find.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is why a custom record zone matters. Like `z`, called Notes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now the iPad must hear about new notes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add a CKSubscription, like `s` in our code. It asks CloudKit to send a push when records change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the CKSubscription wakes the other device?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Then it fetches the changes from the record zone in the private database.
Personal notes belong in the private database.
